# Linkedin post scraper

The Apify actor [`curious_coder/linkedin-post-search-scraper`](https://apify.com/curious_coder/linkedin-post-search-scraper) as typed Telo kinds, generated from its build **1.3.60**. The module's version is that build number, and every run it starts is pinned to exactly that build, so the input types below are the ones the actor really runs with.

Scrape linkedin posts or updates from linkedin post search results.
Supports advanced linkedin search filters.
Extract posts from any linkedin member

## Pricing

Pay per event — Actor Start $0.0005, result $0.0005 (Free-plan prices; paid plans pay less). Cap the spend with `maxTotalChargeUsd`.

Runs are charged to the Apify account whose token the `ApifyClient` holds. See the [Store page](https://apify.com/curious_coder/linkedin-post-search-scraper) for current prices.

## Import

```yaml
imports:
  Actor: oci://ghcr.io/telorun/apify/curious-coder-linkedin-post-search-scraper@1.3.60#sha256-…
```

Pin the digest with `telo upgrade`. The module re-exports `ApifyClient`, so it is the only import needed.

## Usage

```yaml
kind: Actor.ApifyClient
metadata: { name: apify }
token: !cel "secrets.apifyToken"
---
kind: Actor.Run          # or Actor.Start for runs longer than 5 minutes
metadata: { name: scrape }
client: !ref apify
maxTotalChargeUsd: 1     # optional: timeout, memory, maxItems, maxTotalChargeUsd
---
kind: Run.Sequence
metadata: { name: main }
steps:
  - name: scrape
    invoke: !ref scrape
    inputs:
      cookie: []
```

- **`Run`** calls Apify's synchronous endpoint and returns `{ items }`. Apify holds the request open for at most 300 seconds; a longer run fails with HTTP 408.
- **`Start`** starts the run, long-polls it until it finishes, and returns `{ run, items }`. A run that ends `FAILED`, `TIMED-OUT` or `ABORTED` raises `APIFY_RUN_NOT_SUCCEEDED` with the run as `data`.

## Input

Only these fields are accepted — `telo check` rejects any other.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cookie` | array | yes |  | 🍪 Cookies — Cookies are used to authorize the actor with Linkedin  Follow these steps to get the cookies:  - Install [Cookie-Editor](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/cookie-editor/hlkenndednhfkekhgcdicdfddnkalmdm) chrome extension  -  Login to your Linkedin account  -  Click on the extensio |
| `userAgent` | string | yes |  | User agent — [Click here](https://www.google.com/search?q=my+user+agent) to get the user agent info |
| `urls` | array | yes |  | Source URLs — Supported URLs: Linkedin post search URL, Linkedin user or company profile URL, Linkedin post URL |
| `limitPerSource` | integer |  |  | Limit per source — Limit number of posts scraped per source URL |
| `scrapeUntilDate` | string |  |  | Scrape until date — Stop scraping when posts are older than this date (YYYY-MM-DD). Only works when results are sorted by date descending (newest first). For search URLs, add sortBy=%22date_posted%22 to your URL. User and company profile feeds are always newest first. |
| `deepScrape` | boolean |  | `true` | Scrape additional information — Get more information such as likes, comments etc |
| `rawData` | boolean |  | `false` | Get raw data (Advanced) — Push the scraped data directly to the dataset without any processing and filtering. This might be useful if you are looking for some missing data in the dataset |
| `minDelay` | integer |  | `2` | ⏱️ Minimum wait duration — Minimum duration in seconds to wait before scraping next page |
| `maxDelay` | integer |  | `4` | ⏱️ Maximum wait duration — Maximum duration in seconds to wait before scraping next page |
| `proxy` | object | yes |  | Proxy — Choose a proxy from the country where you are logged into LinkedIn |

## Output

The actor publishes no dataset schema, so `items` are untyped objects.
